Maria K: Heads up — over the last 14 days we've seen an uptick in ECC/Xid GPU errors in us-west-2, mostly on older A100 cards. Failure events jumped from ~0.8 -> 2.6 per 10k GPU-hours.
Devin R: Ugh. Is that raw HW failures or driver/kernel noise? Any pattern by host image?
Maria K: Mixed. ~60% correlate with ECC correctable/unhandled and Xid 31/63. The rest are flakey PCI resets with NVLINK warnings. Mostly nodes on image v2024.11.
Sam L: Can you paste the query you ran? want to sanity-check.
Maria K: Sure — prometheus query we used (approx):
```
sum by (region, gpu_model) (increase(gpu_ecc_uncorrectable_total[14d]))
/ (sum by (region, gpu_model) (increase(gpu_gpu_hours_total[14d]))/10000)
```
shows failures per 10k GPU-hours.
Priya N: Thanks. What's our current spare pool for us-west-2? IIRC we keep 20 GPUs (10% of fleet) there.
Devin R: Yes, ~200 active, 20 spare in that region.
Lee T: 2.6/10k hours is ~0.026% per hour -> over a month that's non-trivial. We should model expected replacements and SLO impact.
Maria K: Quick spreadsheet calc I tossed together: for 200 active GPUs, at 2.6/10k hours we expect ~1.25 failures/month. If mean time to replace (including drain+swap) is 3.5 hours, that's ~4.4 GPU-hours of capacity lost monthly -> tiny raw compute, but the issue is burst clustering (multiple failures same week) and preemptive drains.
Sam L: Clustering is the kicker. We saw 4 simultaneous failures last Tuesday when a rack had a degraded power rail.
Priya N: Options: increase spare pool to 30 (15%), or improve detection + hot-swap automation to reduce MTTR to <1h.
Devin R: Automation is cheaper long-term but takes dev time. Do we have historical MTTR distribution? ops-bot: MTTR metrics — median 2.1h, p95 6.8h over last 90d.
Maria K: p95 being 6.8h is what bites us during cluster events. If we cut p95 to 1.5h with better runbooks and remote reboots, we can keep spare pool at 10% and absorb bursts.
Lee T: Also consider regional placement of spares — don't co-locate all spares in a single AZ/rack. That reduces correlated risk.
Sam L: Agreed. Proposal: temp +10% spares in us-west-2 for 30 days while we run automation sprint to reduce MTTR. After that re-evaluate.
Priya N: Cost check: additional 10 GPUs reserved (on Dedicated) ~ $11k/mo (ballpark). Automation sprint ~ 2 engs for 3 sprints -> ~$60k. Break-even if automation avoids one major outage.
Devin R: We also have option B: move oldest A100s out of production into a quarantine pool and schedule replacement with spare budget. That reduces failure rate quickly but increases churn cost.
Maria K: Runbook notes (sketch):
- Detection: alert if Xid 31/63 or ECC errors > 3 in 10m on a host
- Pre-emptive drain: cordon + migrate pods with `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
- Hot-swap: attach queued spare GPU node to same ASG and reassign routing, then decommission node for RMA
- Post-fix: run `nvidia-health-check` + burn-in 2h

Sam L: Can we add canary nodes to detect early rack power issues? like power-sensor checks + extra telemetry?
Maria K: Yes — telemetry team already exposing PSU warnings; we can add a lightweight rule to escalate before GPU errors cascade.
Lee T: Action items:
- Maria: run detailed failure correlation by host-image/firmware and post CSV (due EOD)
- Devin: estimate automation work and PRD for MTTR sprint (due Thu)
- Priya: run cost comparison reserved vs on-demand spares and % impact on unit economics
- Sam: update drain/replace runbook with `kubectl` commands + postmortem template

Priya N: :thumbsup: Does everyone agree on temporary +10% in us-west-2 while we sprint?
Devin R: +1
Sam L: +1
Lee T: +1
Maria K: +1
ops-bot: scheduled change: reserve +10 GPUs in us-west-2 on 1780126800, auto-rollback in 30d (manual confirm required)
Maria K: Thanks all — will share the CSV and a compact exec summary for finance.
Devin R: If we see >5 failures in a week after spares are up, we escalate to replace entire rack set.
Sam L: Noted. I'll add that to runbook as a trigger.
Priya N: Great, can someone drop a short blurb for infra-oncall channel so SREs aren't surprised?
Maria K: Will do. :eyes:
